reviews.title: If You Are Precise in Measuring Your Ingredients, This Is Not the One
reviews.text:
I’m guessing if you just want to scan food and take it as is, or scan barcodes, this app is fine. But things like the voice input are not great usability. 

Sometimes automating everything is not ACTUALLY more convenient. If I am logging by ingredient weight in a recipe, there is no way to go back and edit either. 

So it turns into a giant pain to be able to log actual gram weights in a recipe. 

This is especially painful by voice. Because there is no way to manually enter things after you have weighed them. 

The timeout on the voice function is just too short, with no override. And then you cannot go back and edit. Very user-unfriendly.

I didn’t have it long enough to know whether simple scans would work fairly well, so if that’s what you do primarily, it may work great for you. 

Anyone measuring out ingredients, though, not a good option.

reviews.title: Ruined by Recent User Interface Update
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for about 3 months. It previously had a simple interface that worked well. Unfortunately they recently pushed an update that turned out to be a big downgrade. One example: there’s now a calendar function on the home page that lets you review entries. It shows day/date but not month, so unless you’re scrolling back slowly and paying careful attention it’s easy to lose track of what month you’re looking at. Another example: there used to be a diary page that let you scroll through prior entries. They were in a chronological list, divided into breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack and each entry listed the food and number of calories. Now the diary just shows a big clump of gray rectangles, each representing a food entry. Each rectangle has a title like “chicken” but doesn’t show the calories for that entry. It’s amazingly useless. I think it was done because they want users to take a photo of every item eaten, and if that was done then the diary would show a big array of photos which would look cool (but still not be a useful way to review the information). Other issues: the AI function where you take a picture of your food and the app identifies the item and determines its weight is not reliable. Sometimes it’s amazingly accurate, but other times it gets the type of food wrong or it will misjudge the weight by a factor of two. Also, their food database contains a lot of errors. At least half the time that I scan a barcode I find that the information in SnapCalo

reviews.title: Avoid the half off offer.
reviews.text: This app purported accuracy but is actually inferior to other cheaper options once you opt for the 40 dollar offer. Please be advised that when you are declining membership during the trial, you will be offered a half price sale of 40. Do not fall for that because that is when you will notice a steep decline in accuracy. I’m not sure if this is due to it being processed through an outside server which may be the case since you have to purchase this via email rather than the Apple app store. I am not stating that as factual though, I may be wrong about the reason for the decline in accuracy after falling for the “flash sale”. Still, DO NOT fall for the half off ?scam. Go with another app if you want better accuracy that you would expect for this price.

reviews.title: Redbird67
reviews.text: If I could give this zero stars, I would. First, it started my diary on December, 1969 at 7:00pm. There is an edit icon, but it wouldn’t actually hold any of the changes that I tried to make, kept going back to December, 1969. Next it scanned my food item wrong several times. Kept saying it was yogurt. Finding the delete wasn’t easy and when I finally did get it to delete, it took the information off, but left the picture. All of this in the very first item. I have cancelled my subscription and asked for a refund, but I don’t know if I’ll get it. It either has many bugs that need to be worked out it a better tutorial on hire to use it.

reviews.title: Not great
reviews.text: I appreciate the free trial as it gave me a chance to try it. It’s a great concept, but it’s not good and definitely not worth paying for. You can literally take a photo and tell the AI how many calories are in the food from the package and it still gets it wrong. Sometimes doesn’t even get the nutrition correct when it’s printed in the front of the dam packet! Also buggy in setup.

reviews.title: “Add Missing Food Items” Barcode Scanning Option is Gone with Latest Update
reviews.text: Not sure if this was by design. Searching a food item by keyword does not always yield accurate results and I heavily relied on scanning barcodes for ingredients in a single meal. This is going to make tracking accurately significantly more difficult, as you’re essentially forcing us to scan ingredients as single meal items..I’m really hoping this is just a bug, but I’m really considering switching apps. Please add the barcode scanning feature to missing food items back!!!!

reviews.title: Update broke everythinh
reviews.text: Diary - no longer works, just spins (loading) never gets anywhere. No meal total calories anymore, just individual items only - you can no longer see how many calories you consumed at breakfast unless you add each item up by hand. Poorly tested update, avoid until they rectify.
